topics.name: Perplexity $18B Funding Round
topics.summary: Perplexity in early talks to raise $500M–$1B at an $18B post-money valuation, doubling its December 2024 mark in three months; ARR near $100M; discussed as a potential Apple acquisition target and as evidence of immense investor appetite for AI search.

topics.name: AI Value Accrual: Model vs. Application Layer
topics.summary: Sam Altman told Ben Thompson that a 1B-user destination site will be worth more than a state-of-the-art model in five years, representing a notable shift in his stated position and validating application-layer plays like Perplexity.

topics.name: BigScreen VR Beyond 2 Launch
topics.summary: BigScreen launched its Beyond 2 VR headset at 107 grams with a 116-degree field of view, approaching John Carmack's $100/100g consumer adoption threshold; sold twice as many units as its predecessor; praised by Palmer Luckey.

topics.name: Tornado Cash OFAC Delisting
topics.summary: Tornado Cash removed from OFAC sanctions list in a win for crypto privacy advocates; co-founder Roman Storm still faces up to 45 years in prison with trial in April; Vitalik Buterin rallied support for the founders.

topics.name: Google Acquisition of Wiz for $32B
topics.summary: Google agreed to buy cloud cybersecurity startup Wiz for $32B, the largest software M&A in history; Index Ventures achieved a ~250x seed return and $4.3B total gain; deal requires regulatory approval from the Trump administration.

topics.name: Project Europe (Harry Stebbings)
topics.summary: Harry Stebbings launched a founder collective to counter the 'move to Silicon Valley' narrative; attracted 150+ founders in 3 days and hit the legal cap of 250; views European defense, AI, and deglobalization-driven patriotism as major tailwinds.

topics.name: TechCrunch Acquisition by Regent
topics.summary: TechCrunch sold to Regent media PE firm after years of declining relevance under Verizon and Apollo; Adam Ryan attributed the fall to losing founder-operator journalists, getting stuck between friendly coverage and hard-hitting journalism, and search interest peaking in 2011.

topics.name: Boston Celtics $6.1B Sale
topics.summary: The Celtics sold to unknown PE manager William Chisholm at a record $6.1B for a pro sports franchise; recent NBA rule allowing PE and sovereign wealth fund participation is accelerating valuation growth across the league.

topics.name: DTC E-Commerce Challenges from Tariffs and Consumer Slowdown
topics.summary: Sean Frank and Connor Macdonald described a 'bloodbath' in DTC: tariff uncertainty is freezing capital allocation, consumer confidence hit a multi-month low, Meta ad performance is declining post-iOS 14, and a wave of sub-$10M brand closures is accelerating.

topics.name: Israeli Startup Talent Concentration
topics.summary: Sean Maguire argued Israel's military selection programs, especially Talpiot, create unmatched talent concentration enabling companies like Wiz and Kela to hire 20 elite engineers on day one — a structural advantage increasingly hard to replicate at US universities.

topics.name: M&A Market Outlook
topics.summary: Wiz and Next Insurance exits signal M&A is reopening, but macro tariff uncertainty and European regulatory approval timelines are keeping many potential acquirers cautious about large transactions.

topics.name: SpaceX Starship and NASA's Cost Assumptions
topics.summary: Sean Maguire argued NASA must adapt to Starship's abundant, cheap launch paradigm rather than designing missions for scarce expensive launches; Starship could reduce costs from ~$100K/kg to ~$20/kg.

topics.name: Humanoid Robotics (1X NEO)
topics.summary: 1X announced a research collaboration with Nvidia for their NEO humanoid robot focused on home use; praised for non-threatening aesthetics and compared favorably to Snow Crash-era science fiction.

topics.name: 10X AI Learning App Launch
topics.summary: Blake Anderson launched 10X, a Duolingo-style AI learning platform for coding, marketing, and business skills, live during the episode after 33 days of isolated building; targets the gap between AI capability and consumer literacy.

topics.name: Dual-Use vs. Single-Use Defense Tech Strategy
topics.summary: Sean Maguire called dual-use a 'mirage' often pushed by investors, advising defense founders to lean into where they get genuine product-market pull rather than forcing both enterprise and government use cases early.

topics.name: X as the Everything App
topics.summary: Sean Maguire said X has been broadly underestimated and is entering a phase of visible product acceleration after years of rebuilding infrastructure; payments and new features are rolling out.

topics.name: Delaware Incorporation Exodus
topics.summary: Sequoia publicly backed Elon Musk in his Delaware legal battle and urged founders to leave; Delaware reportedly derives over half of state tax receipts from C-corp filings.

topics.name: Meta Ad Platform Performance Decline
topics.summary: Post-iOS 14 attribution windows shrank from 28 days to 7; Meta increasingly serves warm retargeting audiences rather than driving incremental reach; described by a Meta contact as a 'bloodbath' for growth-oriented DTC brands.

topics.name: BNPL Expansion into Daily Consumer Spending
topics.summary: DoorDash and Klarna's deal to offer food delivery installment payments prompted debate; 15% of Ridge Wallet purchases run through Affirm; hosts expressed concern that burritos on layaway signals dangerous consumer financial stress.

topics.name: Media Talent Retention
topics.summary: Sparked by Alex Earl leaving Alex Cooper's network; discussion of how ESPN retains talent with landmark contracts like Stephen A. Smith's deal and how Barstool kept Big Cat and PFT by understanding their individual needs.
